summary: Oregon's tallest lighthouse, a 93-foot brick tower lit in 1873 after a construction beset by lost boats and impassable roads, still holds its first-order Fresnel lens.

access.note: Within BLM's Yaquina Head Outstanding Natural Area; BLM staff guide visitors through the lighthouse. Check BLM for hours and fees.

notes_for_editor: No Wikipedia cited. Sources disagree and the story says so: start of construction (autumn 1871 per BLM and Maj. Robert's report quoted in NRHP, versus fall 1872 in NRHP text), brick origin (Portland per NRHP; San Rafael per Oregon Encyclopedia and LighthouseFriends), metal work, template tower (Bodie Island per NRHP; Pigeon Point per Oregon Encyclopedia), electrification date (1935 NRHP; early 1930s Encyclopedia; 1933 LighthouseFriends), Zenor's start (1931 per NRHP vs 1932 roster), Plummer's start (30 yrs 4 months in Aug 1907 vs roster 1878). The Light-House Board reports for 1872 and 1879 are cited only as quoted in the NRHP nomination; the local LHB corpus does not hold those years. Wass/Plummer etc. roster lines are from USLHS, not verified in primary registers. The NRHP nomination's 'range 19 miles' has no unit; record says 18 nm. Record says NRHP listed 1993, but nomination certification date is Aug 1992 and the ref number 73002340 suggests a 1973 number; listing date not stated in the story. 1913 newspaper OCR is garbled for the second closed day and visitor count, so omitted. 1900 report page cited by scan page only (printed page unconfirmed). Roster links to Crosby's other stations: Cape Arago id assumed us-or-cape-arago; check it exists. Crosby/Umpqua dates come from LighthouseFriends only.
